mcqs.q: How many epithelial outgrowths does the dental lamina produce for the deciduous teeth?
opts: 10 in the upper and 10 in the lower jaw
mcqs.explain: The dental lamina forms 10 upper + 10 lower outgrowths at the positions of the future deciduous teeth; each begins an enamel organ.

mcqs.q: Tooth development is divided into three stages BASED ON:
opts: The shape of the enamel organ (bud, cap, bell)
mcqs.explain: Based on the shape of the enamel organ, development proceeds through bud, cap and bell stages.

mcqs.q: In the BUD stage, the rounded proliferation of dental-lamina cells is the:
mcqs.explain: In the bud stage the dental-lamina cells proliferate into a rounded bud — the enamel (dental) organ.

mcqs.q: The ectomesenchyme condensed BELOW the enamel organ is the:
mcqs.explain: The dental papilla is the ectomesenchymal condensation below the enamel organ (it forms the pulp and dentin).

mcqs.q: The ectomesenchyme that ENCIRCLES both the enamel organ and dental papilla is the:
mcqs.explain: The dental sac (follicle) encircles both structures and gives rise to the periodontium (cementum, PDL, alveolar bone).

mcqs.q: In the CAP stage, the enamel organ:
opts: Becomes cap-shaped with a short, broad connection to the dental lamina
mcqs.explain: Differential growth makes the enamel organ cap-shaped, with a short broad connection to the dental lamina.

mcqs.q: The 'tooth germ' is composed of:
opts: Enamel organ + dental papilla + dental sac
mcqs.explain: Tooth germ = enamel organ + dental papilla + dental sac; these three are well defined by the cap stage.

mcqs.q: Histodifferentiation of the tooth begins in the:
mcqs.explain: Histodifferentiation (cell specialization) begins in the cap stage as the enamel-organ layers form.

mcqs.q: The OUTER enamel epithelium is composed of:
opts: Cuboidal cells covering the convexity of the enamel organ
Low columnar cells on the concavity
mcqs.explain: The outer enamel epithelium (OEE) is cuboidal cells covering the convex (outer) surface of the enamel organ.

mcqs.q: The INNER enamel epithelium consists of low columnar cells that will become:
mcqs.explain: The inner enamel epithelium (IEE), low columnar cells on the concavity, differentiates into ameloblasts that form enamel.

mcqs.q: The star-shaped cells in the centre of the enamel organ form the:
mcqs.explain: The stellate reticulum is the network of star-shaped cells in the centre of the enamel organ, giving a cushion-like consistency.

mcqs.q: The stellate reticulum cells become star-shaped because central cells:
opts: Secrete hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans that pull water in, stretching the cells
mcqs.explain: Central polygonal cells secrete hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans that draw water from the dental papilla; the cells stretch but stay joined by cytoplasmic processes, becoming star-shaped.

mcqs.q: The enamel knot is a transient condensation found in the:
opts: Central region of the inner enamel epithelium
mcqs.explain: The enamel knot is a condensation of ectodermal cells in the central inner enamel epithelium that may bulge towards the dental papilla.

mcqs.q: The enamel knot and enamel cord are thought to help determine:
opts: The initial position of the first cusp during crown formation
mcqs.explain: These transient structures may set the initial position of the first cusp of the tooth during crown formation.

mcqs.q: The dental papilla ultimately forms the:
mcqs.explain: The dental papilla (ectomesenchyme below the enamel organ) forms the dental pulp and dentin.

mcqs.q: Which structure gives the enamel organ its cushion-like consistency?
mcqs.explain: The water-rich stellate reticulum provides a cushion-like consistency that protects the developing enamel.

mcqs.q: Which enamel-organ layer covers the CONCAVITY?
mcqs.explain: The inner enamel epithelium (low columnar) covers the concavity; the outer enamel epithelium (cuboidal) covers the convexity.

mcqs.q: Each epithelial outgrowth of the dental lamina represents the beginning of a(n):
opts: Enamel organ of a deciduous tooth
mcqs.explain: Each growth from the dental lamina is the beginning of an enamel organ of a deciduous tooth.

mcqs.q: Which physiological stage corresponds to determination of the SHAPE and SIZE of the tooth?
mcqs.explain: Morphodifferentiation is the stage in which the shape and size of the tooth are determined.

mcqs.q: The dental sac (follicle) gives rise to the:
mcqs.explain: The dental sac forms the supporting tissues — cementum, periodontal ligament and alveolar bone.

mcqs.q: Where the inner and outer enamel epithelia meet (the rim of the cap/bell) is called the:
mcqs.explain: The cervical loop is the region where the inner and outer enamel epithelia meet; it is the site where root formation later starts.

saqs.q: Describe the bud stage of tooth development.
saqs.a: Dental-lamina cells proliferate into a rounded bud (enamel organ). Ectomesenchyme condenses below it as the dental papilla and encircles both as the dental sac.

saqs.q: What is the tooth germ, and when is it defined?
saqs.a: Tooth germ = enamel organ + dental papilla + dental sac, well defined by the cap stage, where histodifferentiation begins.

saqs.q: Name the three layers of the cap-stage enamel organ and their cells.
saqs.a: Outer enamel epithelium (cuboidal, convexity), inner enamel epithelium (low columnar, concavity → ameloblasts), and stellate reticulum (star-shaped central cells).

saqs.q: Explain why stellate reticulum cells become star-shaped.
saqs.a: Central cells secrete hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans that pull water in from the dental papilla; the cells stretch but stay joined by cytoplasmic processes, becoming a star-shaped network.

saqs.q: What are the enamel knot and enamel cord?
saqs.a: Transient structures: the enamel knot is a condensation in the central inner enamel epithelium; the enamel cord a strand toward the OEE. They help set the position of the first cusp.

saqs.q: What do the dental papilla and dental sac each form?
saqs.a: Dental papilla → pulp and dentin. Dental sac (follicle) → periodontium (cementum, PDL, alveolar bone).

saqs.q: Distinguish the outer and inner enamel epithelium.
saqs.a: OEE: cuboidal cells on the convexity. IEE: low columnar cells on the concavity, which differentiate into ameloblasts.
